title: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd - 532540 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: TCS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 1.2% QoQ in constant currency, third straight sequential gain, with $12B TCV and 25.3% operating margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹70,698 crore (up 5.4% QoQ in INR, $7.621B up 1.5% QoQ, 1.2% QoQ in constant currency), the third consecutive quarter of sequential growth. Q4 TCV was $12B including three mega deals, and client additions were seen across all revenue bands after about two years. Full-year FY26 revenue declined 2.4% in constant currency to $30.017B, while operating margin reached 25%, a four-year high. Management said the restructuring programme is complete, and the company announced annual increments effective April 1 with top performers getting double-digit increases.

financial_highlights.change: +5.4% QoQ INR; +1.5% QoQ USD; +1.2% QoQ CC

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Grew 1.4% QoQ in constant currency in Q4.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Grew 2.4% QoQ in constant currency in Q4.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew 1.0% QoQ in constant currency in Q4.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Management said the vertical continued to grow in Q4; clients remained cautious amid rate and inflation uncertainty.

segments.name: Consumer Business Group (CBG)
segments.commentary: Saw good growth and a record TCV, with 2 mega deals (Marks & Spencer renewal and expansion, and a US healthcare and pharmacy retailer). Retail globally and TTH UK/EMEA led; CPG and TTH North America declined.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Good growth despite tariff volatility and EV demand recalibration; customers prioritising cost optimisation.

segments.name: Communications, Media and Information (CMI)
segments.commentary: Modest decline in Q4; signed first CMI mega deal, a five-year UK telecom consumer-business contract.

segments.name: Energy, Resources and Utilities (ERU)
segments.commentary: Robust growth overall; Energy and Resources performed well, while Utilities is under stress.

guidance_outlook: No specific revenue or earnings guidance given; management said it is positive on FY27 and on international growth, without quantifying it.
Management expects a regular Q1 and Q2 with a stronger first half, which is the planning assumption.
Wage increments effective April 1 are expected to cost 150-200 bps of margin, similar to the past cycle.
Management expects SG&A to rise both in absolute terms and as a percentage of revenue due to Build-Partner-Acquire investments.
Margins are to be kept within a tighter range, with a longer-term aim of moving toward 26%; rupee depreciation helps but is not guaranteed.
Management expects AI revenue to be net accretive to growth in FY27, aiming to arrest the degrowth in traditional services first.
Combined one-off charges for FY26 were ₹1,300 crore; no one-offs were called out in Q4.
capex_capacity: HyperVault: building toward 1 GW of AI data-centre capacity; anchor workloads seen at 100-200 MW per customer.
OpenAI partnership to build 100 MW capacity with an option to scale to 1 GW.
AMD collaboration on Helios rack-scale AI architecture for high-density AI capacity in India.
Partner ecosystem includes Tata Power, Tata Projects, Tata Communications, GE, Honeywell, ABB and Siemens for EPC, power, cooling and controls.
Land parcel finalisation and customer commitments achieved in Q4; no capex amount disclosed.
demand_pricing: Q4 TCV of $12B included three mega deals: Marks & Spencer, a leading UK telecom operator, and a US healthcare and pharmacy retailer.
FY26 TCV of $40.7B with 5 mega deals; Q4 deal mix was about 50-55% renewals and 40-45% new programmes.
Client additions: 66 accounts above $100M (+4 QoQ), 139 in the $50M+ band (+3), 1,397 in the $1M+ band (+14); every revenue band added clients after about two years.
Pricing: realisations improved, contributing about 40 bps to Q4 margin; management said TCS does not lose deals on pricing.
Clients are shifting from experimentation to industrialised AI, with vendor consolidation and cost optimisation a major theme.
Geopolitical impact so far is limited to the Middle East and travel and transportation; no broad client caution reported outside BFSI-specific caution.
Management said AI deals are 12-16 week rapid builds, and that agentic AI in business process services is gaining traction.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 international growth return to the 3-4% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Krithivasan declined to give a number but said the company is quite positive on FY27 and on international growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is elevated SG&A the new normal, or will it return below 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Seksaria said investments in partnerships, recruitment, training and new businesses will keep SG&A elevated, both in absolute terms and as a share of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Are restructuring costs still to come?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs were called out in Q4; the combined FY26 one-off was ₹1,300 crore. Krithivasan said the restructuring programme is complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected margin impact of wage hikes next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Seksaria said the impact should be similar to the past annual increment cycle, which was 150-200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth being sacrificed for margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Krithivasan said margin is not hurting growth; the margin allows competitive pricing and funds investments such as acquisitions and HyperVault.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI revenue be net accretive to FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Krithivasan said AI is expected to be net accretive in the first year, with the aim of arresting the degrowth in traditional services.

risks_watch: BFSI client caution over interest rates, inflation and central bank actions.
Escalation of geopolitical conflict could cause supply chain disruption and affect travel and transportation and Middle East operations.
Wage increments (150-200 bps margin impact) and higher SG&A could limit margin expansion toward 26%.
AI-led deflation in renewals and existing business may offset AI revenue growth.
Utilities segment stress within ERU, and CPG and TTH North America declines within CBG.
HyperVault execution and capex funding, plus dependence on hyperscaler and model-company commitments.
Quarterly seasonality: management expects a stronger first half, which must be delivered.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q4 momentum, order book and FY27 outlook, while cautious on BFSI and macro. Management avoided quantifying FY27 growth and was evasive on how far SG&A will stay elevated.
key_quotes: We are very pleased to announce third consecutive quarter of sequential growth.
We delivered a strong 1.2% sequentially on a constant currency (CC) basis, in the backdrop of intensifying geopolitical conflicts and macro-economic uncertainty.
We don't lose deals on pricing.
We'd like to move towards 26%, but on a longer-term basis.

adds.what: HyperVault AI data-centre capacity building toward 1 GW; OpenAI partnership to build 100 MW with option to scale to 1 GW

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management expects a regular Q1 and Q2 with stronger 1H and is positive on FY27 without quantifying it, backed by Q4 TCV of $12B (three mega deals) and client additions, while the AI data-centre capacity (HyperVault toward 1 GW, OpenAI 100 MW) is still in planning with no capex or timing disclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Wage increments cost 150-200 bps and SG&A is set to rise as a share of revenue, offsetting the ~40 bps pricing benefit in Q4; management's 26% aim is explicitly long-term and 'tighter range' implies little near-term expansion from 25.3%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: HyperVault is building toward 1 GW of AI data-centre capacity with an OpenAI 100 MW partnership (option to scale to 1 GW), but no capex amount or commissioning timing was disclosed and land and customer commitments were only finalised in Q4.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 TCV of $12B (with three mega deals) and client additions in every revenue band (66 accounts above $100M, +4 QoQ) support a stronger first half, but the 1.2% QoQ CC growth and FY26 CC decline of 2.4% mean the pickup is not yet proven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Land parcel and customer commitments were achieved in Q4 and the partner ecosystem is in place, but no capex amount has been disclosed, so a formal capex figure may follow once funding and anchor contracts firm up.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue or earnings guidance was given, and management declined to quantify FY27 growth, so there is no base to raise; Q4 CC growth was only 1.2% QoQ.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Wage increments effective April 1 are guided at a 150-200 bps margin hit and SG&A is rising, while BFSI clients remain cautious and FY26 CC revenue fell 2.4%, so the 1H-weighted plan has to be delivered.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Agentic AI in business process services is gaining traction and AI deals run as 12-16 week rapid builds with AI annualised revenue above $2.3B, but no specific named product launch or date was given.

rows.label: Record Q4 TCV and mega-deal wins
rows.why: Q4 TCV was $12B including three mega deals (Marks & Spencer, a UK telecom operator, a US healthcare and pharmacy retailer) and FY26 TCV reached $40.7B across 5 mega deals, providing revenue visibility into FY27.

rows.label: Restructuring programme complete
rows.why: Management said the restructuring is complete; the combined FY26 one-off charge was ₹1,300 crore and no one-offs were called out in Q4, so the cost drag should not recur.

rows.label: AI-led deflation in renewals
rows.why: Brief flags AI-led deflation in renewals and existing business as a risk that could offset AI revenue growth, with Q4 deal mix at about 50-55% renewals.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q4 momentum, the $12B TCV, client additions and FY27 positioning, and cautious on BFSI and macro; analysts pushed on FY27 international growth, how long SG&A stays elevated (above 15%), and the margin hit from wage hikes, and management declined to quantify these.
